name: Bold white + accent word
oneliner: Chunky white captions that pop in word by word, with one key word in your accent color.
description: Bold white words with a dark outline pop in as you say them. The one word that matters most lights up in your accent color. The fastest caption look: no cut-out needed.
prompt: Fast caption pass: render with engines/captions.py, which draws exactly this look. Burn in word-level captions from draft.words.json, VERBATIM. Never paraphrase; only fix a mis-heard word and list each fix in the plan. Pure fillers (um, uh) stay off the caption track. Groups of up to 3 words (profile captions.max_words_per_line, passed as --max-words), breaking at punctuation and at pauses over 0.35s. Type: the brand font file if the profile has one (--font, family {{font.display}}), else bundled Inter; weight 800; about 90px at 1080 wide (--font-size to change it); white; tracking -1%; a dark #121212 outline plus a soft shadow 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.45). Exactly ONE accent word in the whole reel, in {{brand.accent}} (--accent-color) with a small 1.14x pulse: pass the noun or number that carries the main idea, as spoken, with --accent (else the longest content word is used). Position: centered, top of the text at y=1152 (60% of the height), 6% side margins, clear of the top 220px and the bottom 320px; keep groups short so they stay off the right 140px button rail. Each word pops in on its own start time: 140ms, scale 0.86 to 1.0 with an 18px rise, back-out ease. A group stays until the next one starts or 0.6s after its last word. Do NOT highlight more than one word, do NOT add boxes, karaoke fill or emojis, and do NOT uppercase everything.
